BLOCKER: `Chain` orders auth/role-gate OUTSIDE quota (executes auth → roleGate → timeout → bodyLimit → quota), so 401/403/503 responses never touch the global token bucket or concurrency semaphores; `TestAuthMiddlewareRunsBeforeQuota` asserts this. AC states "the global bucket always applies and is the hard anti-evasion control", yet unauthenticated brute-force/flood traffic (the exact evasion vector) is entirely uncounted.

Same ordering means oversized-body 413 rejections and role-gate 503 storms also bypass the global bucket, so the advertised 413/429/504 quota counters under-report the attack traffic the quotas exist to bound.

`artifactGet`/`artifactContent` call `svc.Get(r.Context(), id)` / `FetchContent(r.Context(), id)` directly instead of `s.dbCtx(r)`, so DB/object reads on those paths are bounded by the 30s request timeout, not the configured 5s DB timeout (AC: DB 5s bound on every handler).
MAJOR: `GET /metrics` is wrapped in `adminOnly` (docs: "admin bearer ... send the admin token"), making it un-scrapeable by a standard Prometheus job without distributing the admin secret, and it exposes histograms/gauges where AC requires "/metrics (counters only)".

Graceful drain is `max(WriteTimeout, 30s)` = 180s, not the AC's explicit "drains in-flight work on graceful shutdown (30s)"; the docs silently rewrite the requirement instead of flagging the divergence.

`RoleGuard.RecheckLoop` latches closed on ANY recheck error, including transient DB blips, forcing 503 on all data-plane routes for up to `PF_EDP_ROLE_RECHECK` (5m); violation vs. transient failure are conflated.

`config/env-flags.json` is wholesale re-indented (490-line diff) in the same change as the real flag additions — high merge-conflict cost and obscured review of the 40+ new entries in a shared, cross-team registry.
MINOR: `EnvelopeFallback` intercepts every 404/405, replacing handler-specific messages ("artifact not found" → "not found") and discarding body writes; specificity is lost even when the handler produced a correct envelope.
`s.fail` replaces all 4xx messages with `safeStatusMessage`, degrading diagnostics AC never asked to genericize (e.g. `errTenant`'s "tenant query parameter is required" becomes "invalid request").
`TestEnvFlagDefaultsMatch` does `t.Skip` when `config/env-flags.json` is unreachable, so registry/code drift can pass vacuously in CI.
Tenant-cap eviction scans at most 64 random map entries per admission; if those are active, new tenants get 429 despite evictable idle buckets existing elsewhere.
`/artifacts` still fully buffers each upload (`io.ReadAll`) in memory — up to 64 MiB × 10 global concurrency.
AC lists "pool saturation" among /metrics counters, but only `edp_db_pool_*` gauges are emitted; no saturation/denial counter exists.
Auth is enforced twice per request (`authMiddleware` + `adminOnly`) — redundant constant-time compares and two divergent auth paths to maintain.
NIT: Envelope adds a `version` field beyond AC's literal `{"error":{...}}` shape (documented, but the AC text was not updated).
`boolean`/`flagEnabled` and `adminOnly`/`authorize` are small parallel implementations of the same parsing/auth concepts.
Metrics gauges are mutated at scrape time inside the shared registry rather than sampled by a collector.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-tested Go implementation of the guardrails (config validation, envelope, injected-clock quota, shared pool, role fail-closed), but the middleware ordering defeats the AC's "global bucket always applies" anti-evasion guarantee for unauthenticated traffic — the single most important control in this item.

Top risks: quota bypass on auth/role-gate 401/503 paths, /metrics behind an admin token with a counters-only AC violation, 30s-vs-180s shutdown divergence, and DB reads on artifact GET paths not bounded by the 5s DB timeout.
Recommend re-ordering quota outside auth (or double-counting at both layers) and reconciling the AC with the documented deviations before merge.
